hypothesis: Straightest mesh geodesics converge to smooth geodesics; the length (metric) error is O(h^2) on inscribed meshes, the lateral error decreases at least like O(h) but not as a clean power law, and edge-graph distances do not converge.
input_data: graph distances from vertex 0 on icosphere levels 1-4; heat-method distances on levels 1-3
mathematical_model: Inscribed icosphere: chord/arc metric error O(h^2). Lateral error of a straightest geodesic is driven by the imbalance of vertex curvature point masses on either side of the path (a discrepancy sum), so its order is not a single power law. Prism cylinder: development circumference 2nR sin(pi/n) gives L cos(alpha) (a / sin a - 1) ~ L cos(alpha) pi^2 / (6 n^2), plus a chord-position term atan(s tan a) - s a of relative size O(1/n). Edge graph at a valence-5 source: floor sqrt(5) - 2.
numerical_result: Sphere (levels 2-7): length-defect order 2.00, endpoint order 1.63 (pairwise 1.59, 2.02, 1.52, 1.08, 2.11), cross-track 1.56 (pairwise 1.37, 2.06, 1.40, 1.02, 2.12), finest mean endpoint error 1.16e-04 rad; 1 of 36 per-trace level steps increase the endpoint error. Cylinder: order 2.024, helix error equals the closed form to 4.1e-15, n^2 error / C = 1.0770, 0.9479, 1.0178, 0.9889, 0.9936. Edge Dijkstra max signed relative error 0.1449, 0.2108, 0.2296, 0.2344 (levels 1-4), Aitken 0.23613 vs sqrt(5) - 2 = 0.23607; Steiner k=3 max |relative error| 0.0307, 0.0082, 0.0110, 0.0138; heat-method order 1.01.
observation_model: Endpoint angle on the unit sphere after radial projection; helix error on the cylinder surface; relative distance error against the great-circle distance.

title: Measure convergence under mesh refinement.
uncertainty: Deterministic; fitted orders depend on the chosen levels and geodesics (six directions), and the pairwise local orders of the endpoint error range over about 1 to 2. The lateral-error order is an empirical slope, not a proved rate.
unresolved_assumptions: Endpoint-error order is empirical and depends on how geodesic directions align with lattice rows.
Heat-method time step t = h^2 as recommended by Crane et al.; other choices change the rate.
The edge-graph floor is derived for the valence-5 source used here; other sources have other floors (1/cos(pi/6) - 1 at regular valence 6).
